claims.subject: fujitsu-tofu-interconnect identity, topology, rank mapping, places, grain
claims.reason: Ajima et al., Tofu: Interconnect for the K computer (2012), pp. 280–282, §§1–3.4, describes the controller, six-dimensional topology, and 3D rank mapping; University of Tokyo Oakleaf notice p. 1 independently identifies deployed 6D Tofu and Kashiwa.

claims.subject: original Tofu 2009 publication event
claims.reason: Ajima, Sumimoto and Shimizu, Computer 42(11), November 2009, abstract states six-dimensional topology and three-phase routing. Only the abstract was accessible; no broader article claims are admitted.

claims.subject: original Tofu K 2011 deployment and Oakleaf 2012 adoption events
claims.reason: TOP500 K system entry and 06/2011 row document benchmarked Tofu system. University of Tokyo 2 April 2012 operator notice, p. 1, dates Oakleaf operation and specifies 4,800 compute nodes connected by 6D Tofu.

claims.subject: fujitsu-tofu-interconnect-2 JAXA April 2015 adoption and Japan place extension
claims.reason: JAXA Japanese operator chronology, JSS2 overview, 第2期, explicitly dates the start of operation of part of SORA-MA to April 2015; Takaki, SORA-MA evaluation, p. 53, §2, identifies deployed FX100 and Tofu2. This is distinct from existing June NIFS event.

claims.subject: Tofu2 adapts original Tofu
claims.reason: Ajima Hot Interconnects 2014 slides 1, 4 and 7 explicitly compare generations, controller integration and six axes; the Tokyo FX10 operator notice p. 1 and JAXA operator Takaki p. 53 independently describe each operational generation, while Takaki explicitly states FX100 inherits K and FX10 system architecture. The accepted relation is limited to topology and integration; application measurements do not isolate network inheritance.

claims.subject: Tofu2 candidate from K
claims.reason: Narrowed question preserves unresolved routing, hardware barrier and rank-mapping internals; neither Takaki p. 53 nor RIKEN FY2015 §1.3.1 proves exact implementation inheritance. Its status remains candidate.

claims.subject: K requires original Tofu
claims.reason: Ajima 2012 pp. 280–282 describes K interconnect; TOP500 K entry and June 2011 row identify configuration; Ueno et al. 2017 §§5.1–5.2, 6.2 evaluate topology-aware work on operating K. Scope is the actual built configuration, not a universal statement about all possible supercomputers.

claims.subject: K requires VIIIfx
claims.reason: TOP500 K system and June 2011 row identify SPARC64 VIIIfx; Ishikawa and Kanamori, Porting DDalphaAMG solver to K computer, §§3–4, describe measured SIMD use by independent users on K. Scope is the built K configuration.

claims.subject: fujitsu-sparc64-viiifx identity, description, aliases, grain, event May 2009
claims.reason: PC Watch first-hand report dated 14 May 2009 records VIIIfx/Venus package publicly displayed at Fujitsu Forum in Tokyo. Bounded date avoids claiming event start; Maruyama, Hot Chips 2009 slides 4–7 and 13, describes HPC-ACE extensions and eight-core processor.

claims.subject: VIIIfx Hot Chips presentation event
claims.reason: Maruyama dated original author slides 25 August 2009, slides 1, 3–7, 12–17 and 20, specify the processor and include hardware-measured results.

claims.subject: sparc-v9 identity, compatibility, publication event
claims.reason: SPARC International Architecture Manual Version 9, preface and §§1, 1.2.1, 3, documents 64-bit architecture and qualified user ABI compatibility; its errata identifies the first 1994 printing. Inspected manual mirror is a later revision and is identified as such.

claims.subject: VIIIfx adapts SPARC V9
claims.reason: SPARC V9 manual and Fujitsu/Sun JPS1 Commonality §1 and §3.1 document specification relationship; Maruyama Hot Chips 2009 slides 4–7 and 13 identify SPARC-V9/JPS plus HPC-ACE, including SIMD and extended registers. This is an instruction-architecture relationship, not proof of reused processor hardware.

claims.subject: lane report and new source metadata
claims.reason: Report records exact scope, independent experimental use, source limitations and unresolved AP1000/AP3000 and lower-level interconnect lineage. Reviewed source locators match claims; 2009 Tofu full paper remains abstract-only and performance comparisons retain their stated system and software conditions.

corrections: JAXA English chronology merely said added in April; revised to Japanese operator original explicitly stating start of operation.
Replaced dead Fujitsu source URLs with working original conference, operator, joint-specification and coauthor-hosted copies; bounded VIIIfx exhibition to a 14 May eyewitness report.
Corrected source locators and avoided overreading 3D rank mapping.
deferred: No AP1000 or AP3000 to Tofu inheritance admitted: shared torus topology, vendor and personnel do not prove transmission. IPSJ Computer Museum AP1000 and AP3000 entries and Tridgell ANU thesis appendix B.1 establish historical comparators.
Specific Tofu2 routing, hardware barrier and rank-mapping internals and VIIIfx microarchitectural reuse remain candidate research.
Full 2009 Tofu article unavailable; only its author abstract and journal metadata support the bounded 2009 event.
